text:
pagerbot: PAGED @oncall_sre (Anne) — Elevated 5xx rate from runtime pool 'inference-prod-4' (alerts: gateway_5xx_rate > 12% over 5m). Incident severity: P1.

Anne (oncall_sre): I'm on it, joining. Can someone confirm which model(s) are affected?

Ryan (runtime): seeing a spike of segfaults and OOMs on model-runner v2.3.1 when SeqLen > 2048. Logs show repeated `SIGSEGV` in libtorch / CUDA kernels.

Jai (ml_ops): affected customer traffic: a handful of high-QPS customers pinned to prod-4 pool + some hostnames hitting hosted API. Initial estimate ~8% of overall requests impacted, but one enterprise tenant reported 30% errors.

Maya (eng_lead): @ryan prioritize mitigation over root cause for now. What's the safest quick fallback?

Ryan (runtime): two options: 1) auto-failover by routing to runner v2.2.8 (no JIT kernel changes) — risk: slightly higher latency but stable; 2) route to smaller quantized variant (q4_0) — risk: quality regression.

Anne (oncall_sre): Start canary routing to v2.2.8 for 10% of traffic from the affected pool. Jai, can you flip routing and monitor?

Jai (ml_ops): doing now. Command: `redwood route update --pool inference-prod-4 --fallback v2.2.8 --pct 10`. Pushing...

ops_bot: route update accepted. Changes propagated to control-plane.

Jai (ml_ops): 10% routed to v2.2.8. 1 minute after change: gateway 5xx down from 12.4% -> 9.7%.

Emily (CS): Customer EmilyCorp reports partial outages affecting chat autosaves, flagging elevated error pages. I'm drafting comms: "we're mitigating, routing traffic to fallback runtime; no data loss expected."

Anne (oncall_sre): Good. Meanwhile Ryan, can we hotfix the crashing hosts? Any quick kernel/log artifacts to collect?

Ryan (runtime): attaching key snippets — looking at node ids: inf-4a-03..inf-4a-07. Repro on a smaller test job using the long-context harness: got `cudaMalloc` failures then segfault. Kernel logs show GPU driver resets. Suspect a quantized kernel regression in v2.3.1's fused attention.

Ryan (runtime): logs:
```
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: cublasStatusInternalError: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: SIGSEGV at 0x7f8b4c1a2f (libcudart.so)
[2026-03-15T21:12:04Z] kernel: NVRM: GPU lost: Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus
```

Tom (infra): I'm seeing host-level OOM events around same timestamps, pages swapped, and then evictions. Hosts show `oom_reaper` activity. We're isolating nodes from autoscaler to prevent churn.

Anne (oncall_sre): Good. Jai keep increasing fallback pct if errors don't drop. Also enable prefix/KV cache bypass for affected routes to reduce memory pressure.

Jai (ml_ops): incrementing to 40% now. `redwood route update --pool inference-prod-4 --pct 40`.

ops_bot: route update accepted.

Jai (ml_ops): 40% routed. Gateway 5xx -> 6.2% after 90s. Latency for fallback increased by ~35ms p50.

Maya (eng_lead): plan: (A) complete traffic shift to v2.2.8 if stability continues; (B) hotpatch v2.3.1 with reverted fused-attention kernel; (C) post-incident rollback plan for pinned customers. Agree?

Ryan (runtime): agree. For hotpatch we need to build v2.3.1-hotfix and roll to a small canary subset. I can prepare build but will need infra to deploy to a limited set.

Tom (infra): Can provision 3 replacement nodes (no GPU driver update) for canary. Provisioning now.

Emily (CS): which customers to notify proactively? I have a list of 6 enterprise tenants with elevated error traces. I'll send targeted status to the ones with >10% error and offer to move them to Dedicated.

Anne (oncall_sre): Emily, please post a status in #status-updates with ETA ~45m for mitigation. Also set incident ETA for postmortem.

Emily (CS): posting now.

ops_bot: STATUS: "Mitigation in progress — routing to fallback runtime v2.2.8. Next update in 30m."

Ryan (runtime): hotfix build complete. `v2.3.1-hotfix` with fused-attn revert. Pushing small canary to nodes inf-4a-09..inf-4a-11.

Tom (infra): canary nodes up and running. Deploy command: `deploy runtime v2.3.1-hotfix --nodes inf-4a-09..11 --env prod`.

ops_bot: deployment initiated.

Anne (oncall_sre): monitoring telemetry: kernel restarts count, coredumps, 5xx rate, and per-tenant error ratio. Please upload any coredumps to `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/3959876543/` with metadata tags `incident=3959876543` and `node=<hostname>`.

Ryan (runtime): uploaded two core dumps + `strace` output for one crash: `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/3959876543/inf-4a-05-core.tgz` Also traced a trace_id: `trace-8a7f3d2c` — correlated with customer EmilyCorp request.

Tom (infra): checking driver versions: all affected nodes are on nvidia-driver 525.89.02; provisioning nodes are same. Might be a subtle memory leak under certain CUDA workloads. I'll open a ticket with driver vendor if hotfix does not help.

Jai (ml_ops): hotfix canary shows 0 segfaults after 7 minutes, 5xx rate on canary <0.5%.

Anne (oncall_sre): Excellent. Gradually promote hotfix to 50% of formerly affected pool while reducing v2.2.8 fallback. Keep an eye on tail latency and quality regressions.

Jai (ml_ops): promoting to 50%. `redwood route promote --pool inference-prod-4 --target v2.3.1-hotfix --pct 50`.

ops_bot: promotion accepted.

Jai (ml_ops): 50% done. Overall 5xx dropped to 1.1% within 4m. Enterprise customers reporting recovery.

Emily (CS): EmilyCorp confirms errors dropped to <2% and chat autosaves returning. Posting customer update and offering session with solutions engineer.

Maya (eng_lead): good job. Keep hotfix roll until 100% if metrics stable for 15m. Also schedule postmortem with SRE, runtime, ml_ops, infra, and CS.

Anne (oncall_sre): marking incident as active mitigated. CCS (customer-impact summary): - Peak 5xx 14% across pool; impacted ~12% of requests; enterprise worst-case 30% for EmilyCorp; no data loss; mitigation: route to stable runtime v2.2.8 then v2.3.1-hotfix; root cause suspected regression in fused-attention kernels causing GPU resets and host OOM.

ops_bot: Incident log updated. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update in 30m.

Ryan (runtime): notes for postmortem: collect perf traces, reproduce with long-context harness, add extra guardrails in runtime to reject huge seq lengths with safety fallback, and add memory limit enforcement per-request.

Tom (infra): follow-ups: pin driver version check in autoscaler, add node health filter to avoid scheduling new runners on nodes with kernel OOM history, and improve coredump collection automation.

Jai (ml_ops): follow-ups: extend canary window on future deployments for v2.3.x, add quantized kernel unit tests targeting long seqs.

Maya (eng_lead): action owners: Ryan -> runtime fix + tests; Tom -> infra hardening; Jai -> rollout policy changes; Emily -> customer comms; Anne -> lead postmortem. Meeting scheduled: 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC.

Anne (oncall_sre): closing chat for now. If 5xx stays <1.5% for 30m we'll move to post-incident. Thanks everyone. :tada:
